name: Question 19
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/c7d87ad16ee6ab95b66bc2609707236c281407e473f5b834f484f002736c794c.png)

Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}y\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9$ for $z\ge 0,$ shown above.
worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $3$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14096572/assets/77791875e8b70bc528e4c765971d21c0567be80ffe58f7b1813d6be44db6bf33.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 3,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}y\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{3}\,d\rho  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{3}{\rho }^{3}\,d\rho  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[ϕ-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2ϕ]}_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi /2}\cdot [-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot {[\frac{1}{4}{\rho }^{4}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{2}-0)\cdot (-1+1)\cdot \frac{1}{4}(81-0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot 0\cdot \frac{81}{4} \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
